user_consequence: A VoiceOver/screen-reader user on Stats, CoachHelm Home, or Triage Desk (every screen built on the shared StageRouter) has the ENTIRE swapped panel's rendered text announced as a live-region update on every stage change, and potentially re-announced on any subsequent re-render inside that panel that mutates visible text (a metric refreshing, a retry completing) -- not just the intended 'you navigated' cue. This is on top of (not instead of) the router's own explicit focus-move to the panel, which already gives AT users a navigation cue by itself.
mechanism: StageRouter.tsx wraps its entire swappable content region in a page/region-wide aria-live: `<div data-slot="stage" className="relative min-h-[320px]" aria-live="polite">` (line 166), with the active view's full subtree (`data-slot="stageview"`, tabIndex=-1) rendered directly inside it. A separate useEffect (lines 134-140) already calls `stageViewRef.current?.focus({preventScroll:false})` on every activeKey change (skipped on first mount) -- the correct, narrower mechanism for announcing a stage swap to AT. The aria-live wrapper is redundant with that focus move and, because it spans the whole content region rather than a small status string, will cause verbose/whole-panel readout for any live region content change within the swapped view, not a scoped 'switched to X' announcement. StatsSpineStage.tsx:599 and PlayerCoachHelmHome/TriageDesk mount real, data-bearing panels (drill breakdowns, bento cells, task lists) inside this exact wrapper, so this is not a decorative/dead code path.
expected: Per plan Section 6/A12 item 1: 'Whole-page live regions can be disruptive.' A stage swap should be announced once, narrowly (e.g. via the existing focus move, or a single small visually-hidden status string), not by making the entire swapped panel's content a live region.
actual: The generic content wrapper for every StageRouter consumer (Stats, CoachHelm Home, Triage Desk) carries aria-live="polite" on the full panel, redundant with an already-correct focus-move mechanism in the same file.
proposed_fix: Remove aria-live from the `data-slot="stage"` wrapper (the tabIndex=-1 focus move at lines 134-140 already gives AT users the navigation cue) or replace it with a small dedicated visually-hidden `role="status"` element that announces only a short 'Now viewing <label>' string, decoupled from the panel's actual content subtree.
accessibility_check: WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages) intent is to keep live-region announcements narrow/predictable; wrapping arbitrary rich content is the documented anti-pattern this finding cites. NOT independently re-verified with an axe/AT run (NOT_RUN, no runtime).

user_consequence: A player who has set 'Reduce Motion' (a documented vestibular-safety accessibility need) still gets a large (80px), continuously looping ease-in-out spinning ring on the 'Submitting round' screen -- the one animation in this exact file that is NOT gated, while every other transition in the same component correctly collapses to instant/no-motion for the same user. This is not a hypothetical drift: the repo's own product-wide reduced-motion regression gate could not have caught it, and would not catch a recurrence, because of a structural blind spot described below.
mechanism: FairwayRoundSubmitOverlay.tsx imports `useReducedMotion` from framer-motion (line 20) and correctly gates every framer-motion transition in the file on `prefersReducedMotion` (lines 68, 240, 258, 269, 278, 300, 353, 412 all read `prefersReducedMotion ? {duration:0} : ...`). But the submitting-state progress ring (lines 419-437) is a raw Tailwind arbitrary-value CSS animation -- `className="... animate-[submitRingSpin_2s_ease-in-out_infinite] text-accent-500"` (line 433) driving a `@keyframes submitRingSpin` (line 474) -- entirely outside framer-motion, with no `motion-reduce:` variant and no `prefersReducedMotion` check anywhere near it. It is the ONLY unguarded animation in a file whose author otherwise consistently applies the gate. Separately: the repo's own product-wide gate for this exact defect class, `scripts/__tests__/motion-reduced-motion-coverage.test.mjs` (referenced by `src/app/admin/__tests__/admin-motion-guard-coverage.test.ts`'s doc-comment as the reason admin doesn't need its own product-wide check), is not referenced in `package.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, or any `.github/workflows/*.yml` file (independently verified: `grep -rl motion-reduced-motion-coverage` across all three surfaces returns nothing) -- so it never runs in CI or via any npm script. Even if it did run, its detection method (`scripts/__tests__/motion-reduced-motion-coverage.test.mjs:122-131`) only checks whether a file that imports framer-motion contains the string `useReducedMotion` or `prefers-reduced-motion` ANYWHERE in its raw source -- a file-level presence check, not a per-animation assertion. FairwayRoundSubmitOverlay.tsx would PASS that check today (it does call useReducedMotion, for its OTHER animations) despite shipping this one ungated raw-CSS loop, because the gate cannot see that a specific non-framer-motion className was never conditioned on the hook's return value.
expected: Per plan Section 9.3/T22: reduced-motion/haptics-off users complete the essential task without depending on a sensory cue the app promised to suppress; per Section 8.3 motion should be purposeful and preference-aware everywhere, not file-by-file best-effort.
actual: One infinite, ease-in-out looping animation ships unconditionally to reduced-motion users on a core round-completion screen, and the repository's own regression gate for this defect class is both unwired and structurally unable to catch this specific pattern (a raw CSS animate-* class living alongside an already-gated framer-motion file).
proposed_fix: Gate the ring: add a `motion-reduce:animate-none` Tailwind variant (matching the pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase, e.g. StageRouter.tsx's `motion-safe:animate-[fade-up...] motion-reduce:animate-none`) or condition the className on `prefersReducedMotion` directly, since the hook is already in scope. Separately (routed to A00/A03 as a shared-gate request, not an A12 edit): wire `scripts/__tests__/motion-reduced-motion-coverage.test.mjs` into `npm run test:all` or CI, and extend its detector to also flag a raw Tailwind `animate-[...]`/`animate-spin`/`animate-pulse`/`animate-bounce`/`animate-ping` utility that lacks a `motion-reduce:` companion, independently of whether the file happens to import framer-motion elsewhere -- the admin-side gate (`admin-motion-guard-coverage.test.ts`) already implements exactly this per-utility check for `src/app/admin/**`; the product-wide gate does not.
accessibility_check: WCAG 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions, AAA) and the app's own stated reduced-motion contract are both violated by this one loop; every other motion in the same file correctly honors the preference, confirming this is an omission, not a deliberate exception.

user_consequence: A screen-reader user entering or correcting hole data on the round-setup screen gets zero indication, at the field level, of which hole/input is invalid -- there is no sighted-only shortcut being missed here; the mechanism to point at a specific field simply does not exist for anyone. Worse, for the two skip-to-tracking paths this program has already found (A05-008 cloud-tee padding, A05-015 recent-courses quick-pick), the invalid 0-yardage hole data is never validated or surfaced AT ALL -- not even the one generic banner that exists for other errors -- because both paths bypass the hole-configuration screen and the one validation function that runs before persisting a round entirely.
mechanism: FairwayHoleConfig.tsx (`grep -n "aria-invalid|aria-describedby|error"` -> zero matches in the whole file) never renders a per-hole/per-field error, never sets `aria-invalid`, and never associates any input with a description via `aria-describedby`. The ONLY error surface in the entire round-creation flow is one generic `InlineNotice` in FairwayNewRoundEntry.tsx (lines 997-1000, title fixed as 'Unable to start round'), fed by a single `error: string | null` prop from new-round-client.tsx's `validateBeforeStart()` (lines 1208-1234). That function validates course name, qualifier selection, course rating (50.0-85.0) and slope (55-155) ranges, and round date -- it NEVER inspects any hole's `par`/`yardage` value. So even the generic, field-agnostic banner cannot fire for a hole-data problem; the two skip-to-tracking gates in new-round-client.tsx (handleTeePick's par-4/yardage-0 padding at lines ~1069-1078, gated by the cloud-pick check `h.par > 0` at line ~1334; and handleQuickPickConfirm's `.some(h => h.yardage > 0)` gate at line 1017) both route straight to `setStep('tracking')` with zero validation layer in between -- sighted and screen-reader users alike get no error, banner, or field marker at all for this specific defect class.
expected: Per plan Section 6/A12 item 1 (error-to-field association) and Section 9.2: an invalid field is identifiable programmatically (aria-invalid + aria-describedby) to AT users, and a defect that produces bad committed data has SOME visible/announced error state, not silent success.
actual: No field-level ARIA error association exists anywhere in the hole-editing UI, and the one validation function that could surface a hole-data problem never checks hole data, so the two known skip-to-tracking defects (A05-008, A05-015) produce zero error surface for any user, sighted or not.
proposed_fix: When A05's proposed fix lands (real yardage validation before allowing the skip-to-tracking path), pair it with per-field `aria-invalid="true"` and an `aria-describedby` pointing at a visually-adjacent, hole-numbered error string in FairwayHoleConfig.tsx, so the fix is accessible by construction rather than sighted-only.
accessibility_check: WCAG 3.3.1 (Error Identification) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) both require a programmatic error association that is currently absent from this entire flow.

user_consequence: A player with larger fingers or reduced fine-motor precision has a slightly harder time hitting the correct par (3/4/5) button per hole on the round-setup/hole-config screen than they would on any shared-primitive control elsewhere in the app, because this specific custom control is the one place that does not grow on a touch device.
mechanism: FairwayHoleConfig.tsx's per-hole par selector (lines 265-289) is a hand-rolled `<button>` (commented `eslint-disable-next-line helm/no-raw-button -- custom par-selector chip`) sized `h-9 w-9` (line 284) = 36x36 CSS-px, with `gap-1.5` (6px) between the three chips -- no overlap, but no growth path either. By contrast, the shared design-system `IconButton` (button.tsx:264) uses the SAME 36px base for its `sm` size but adds `[@media(pointer:coarse)]:h-11 [@media(pointer:coarse)]:w-11` (44px) specifically for touch devices (button.tsx:261-262's own comment: 'All sizes clear the WCAG 2.2 >=24px minimum; on coarse pointers sm expands to the DoD-preferred >=44px touch target'). Because the par chip is a custom control outside that primitive, it never receives the pointer-coarse bump and stays at 36px on every device, including touch.
expected: Per plan Section 6/A12 item 2: adopt the measured 44x44 CSS-px product touch goal for important controls, while correctly distinguishing it from the WCAG 2.5.8 AA minimum (24x24, with exceptions) so a 36px control is NOT misreported as an AA failure.
actual: 36x36 CSS-px par-selector chips PASS WCAG 2.5.8 AA (36 > 24, no exception needed) but MISS the plan's 44x44 enhanced/product goal and the pointer-coarse pattern the shared IconButton primitive already implements one file away in the same design system -- correctly framed as a P3 craft gap, not an accessibility-conformance failure.
proposed_fix: Either route the par selector through the shared IconButton/segmented-control primitive (which already has the coarse-pointer bump), or add the same `[@media(pointer:coarse)]:h-11 [@media(pointer:coarse)]:w-11` pair directly to this control's className, keeping the 6px gap so three 44px chips (150px) still fit the existing `104px` column width constraint check -- this requires re-measuring the grid template (`grid-cols-[52px_1fr_104px]`, line 257) before landing, since the par column is currently sized for 36px chips, not 44px ones.
accessibility_check: WCAG 2.5.8 AA: PASS (36px > 24px minimum, independently confirmed). WCAG 2.5.5 AAA / plan's 44px product goal: MISS.

user_consequence: If A02-001 (four uncoordinated global reload mechanisms, one of which resets the others' attempt budget on every successful mount) is fixed today, nothing in the automated test suite would catch a regression that reintroduced it. A future change could silently restore the exact P0 behavior A02-001 documents and every existing green test suite would stay green.
mechanism: Independently verified by tracing test coverage for each of A02-001's four cited mechanisms: (1) `src/components/providers/__tests__/StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript.test.ts` exists and its name suggests it covers the recovery script, but reading its actual assertions (lines 20-48) shows it ONLY tests which field (`data.release` vs the removed `data.deploymentId`) the health-check response reads -- it never renders the beforeInteractive script, never simulates a 'Load failed' error, never asserts the MAX_RELOADS budget, and never asserts a dirty-form/unsaved-work guard (there is none to assert, per A02-001). (2) `src/components/providers/ChunkLoadErrorHandler.tsx` -- the component whose UNCONDITIONAL per-mount reset of the `chunk-error-reload` sessionStorage key is the core of A02-001's 'budget resets to zero on every successful hydration' finding -- has NO test file at all (confirmed: `find . -iname 'ChunkLoadErrorHandler*'` returns only the source file). (3) `src/components/errors/RouteErrorBoundary.tsx` -- the third mechanism, which reuses the same sessionStorage key with different (presence/absence vs budget) semantics -- also has NO test file. (4) `src/test/lib/error-logging.test.ts` DOES test `softReloadForStaleServerAction`'s own per-session dedup in isolation (lines 99-192), but never tests the cross-mechanism race A02-001 flags (a single 'stale server action' message matching BOTH mechanism 1's and mechanism 4's classifiers and firing two independent reload attempts), and -- like (1) -- cannot test a dirty-form guard that does not exist in the source.
expected: Per plan Section 16.4: 'draft/unknown-commit tests' and negative T01/T02 coverage should exist as PERMANENT regression coverage once a P0 finding like A02-001 is repaired, so the fix cannot silently regress.
actual: A test file whose name implies T01/T02 coverage tests an unrelated concern; two of the four cited mechanisms (ChunkLoadErrorHandler, RouteErrorBoundary) have no test file whatsoever; the one test that does exercise reload dedup logic does not test the cross-mechanism race that makes A02-001 severe.
proposed_fix: Once A02-001's repair packet lands (single coordinated recovery classifier), add: a test asserting a dirty-form/active-operation guard blocks the reload path; a test asserting the reload attempt budget survives a successful hydration (replacing ChunkLoadErrorHandler's current unconditional reset); and a test that fires the same error message through both the beforeInteractive script's classifier and error-logging.ts's classifier simultaneously and asserts exactly one reload attempt, not two.
